subject: Request: Dedicated serving kickoff — Greylake calendar coordination
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@greylake.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity evaluation — request to schedule

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks — I registered via the self‑signup flow earlier this morning (Greylake AI). We have a pilot coming up and want to scope Redwood's Dedicated offering for production inference. High level: we need a serving setup that can sustain medium‑high throughput for chat-style completion endpoints (roughly 350–450 QPS sustained, with spikes to ~600 QPS) and 95th‑percentile token latency under ~200ms.

Would love to get a short technical kickoff/demo with someone from the capacity team to validate assumptions and confirm whether Reserved capacity is a fit. Ideally we'll cover the model variants you're recommending, autoscale behavior, and a rough timeline for piloting.

Available windows for our team (PST): Oct 14 10:00–11:00, Oct 15 09:00–10:00, Oct 18 afternoon.

Also happy to share sample traffic traces or a small set of prompts in advance if that helps.

Regards,
Priya Shah
Head of Platform — Greylake AI
priya.shah@greylake.ai
+1 (415) 555‑0192

Attachments: none in this message
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@greylake.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity evaluation — request to schedule

Hi Priya — great to hear from you and thanks for the details.

We can absolutely run a focused kickoff to align on throughput/latency expectations and pilot next steps. A couple quick asks so we come prepared:
- Can you confirm whether the 350–450 QPS is per‑model endpoint (single model) or aggregated across multiple endpoints?
- Do you have a target SLA for tail latency (95th or 99th), and is 200ms the firm cutoff?
- If possible, please attach a small sample (100–200 requests) or a simple JSONL workload so Diego can do a pre‑demo capacity sanity check.

Proposed slots (PT):
- Thu Oct 14, 10:00–10:45 PT (fits your first window)
- Fri Oct 15, 09:00–09:45 PT
- Mon Oct 18, 13:30–14:15 PT

I can take the kickoff. Diego will join to cover runtime limits and quick kernel/instance fit, and Ben (AE) will join to cover pricing/commit options for Reserved capacity.

I've attached a short capacity intake form (capacity-intake-form.csv) to collect a few fields that speed up the pre‑demo check. If you can fill the top section (QPS, average tokens per request, peak pattern, preferred region), that'll let Diego simulate a representative load before our call.

If any of the slots work, I'll send a calendar invite and a short agenda.

Thanks — Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior SDR — Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.com

Attachment: capacity-intake-form.csv (stub)

Thanks Evelyn — confirmed answers below and attached a sample workload.

- The 350–450 QPS is for our primary chat endpoint (single model variant) — we may have a second lower‑traffic endpoint later.
- Target tail: 95th percentile < 200ms; 99th should be as low as possible but not required in the kickoff.
- Attached: sample-workload.jsonl (100 lines, anonymized prompts + expected token lengths).

Preferred slot: Thu Oct 14, 10:00–10:45 PT works best for our team. Please send the invite with a Google Meet link.

One other note — our data plane will be in us‑west region; we may require VPC connectivity for pilot evaluation depending on the data classification. We'll flag that during the call.

–Priya

Perfect — Thu Oct 14, 10:00–10:45 PT is booked. Invite sent: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=greylake-dedicated-kickoff-20271014

Agenda (20–25m technical, 15–20m commercial):
- Brief introductions and goals (Priya, Alex)
- Runtime architecture + model variants recommended for your workload (Diego)
- Throughput/latency alignment and preliminary capacity fit (Diego)
- Pilot timeline & reserved capacity options (Ben)
- Next steps / action items (Evelyn)

Diego: we'll take the attached sample-workload.jsonl and run a fast local sizing pass this afternoon. If you can share any traffic shape (burstiness, average tokens per request), that helps tune the sim. I'll upload our capacity checklist after the sizing run — attaching capacity-checklist.pdf for your reference (quick read).

If anything changes on your side, reply and we'll re‑slot. Looking forward to the call.

Evelyn
